transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Edenware), Rajiv Menon (CTO), Tom Brooks (Platform Lead), Sara Kline (Purchasing)

Summary:
Quick check-in on renewal cadence, Edenware asks for a capacity uplift + add EU region, discuss pilot for private/VPC path, security and contract timeline. Agreed to run a short benchmark pilot and send revised pricing.

Topics:
- Current usage and forecast (qps, burst patterns)
- Latency targets vs cost tradeoffs
- EU region activation and data residency needs
- Private / VPC pilot scope and timeline
- Contract amendment and PO timing

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um gonna kick off, uh quick intros? we have about 45 minutes but we'll go til 50 if needed. Maya from Redwood, Owen our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz (Edenware): hi all, lena here, head of ml at edenware. thanks for fitting us in.
[00:23] Rajiv Menon (Edenware): rajiv, cto, i'll jump in on ops and contract bits.
[00:27] Tom Brooks (Edenware): tom, platform lead. happy to go over traffic and dev needs.
[00:31] Sara Kline (Edenware): sara from purchasing. i'll be tracking PO timing.
[00:34] Owen Patel (Redwood): hey, owen, focus on perf and pilot setup. quick agenda: capacity numbers, eu onramp, private pilot, security docs, next steps.

[01:02] Maya: Great. So to start lena you mentioned in email you were seeing steady growth — can you give us the main drivers and what you want from this renewal?
[01:12] Lena: yeah, so main drivers are twofold: increased user-facing summarization and a new analytics assistant feature we expect to hit 30k monthly active queries by q3. We're currently on hosted tier but need predictable throughput and EU residency for a subset of customers. want to lock in committed capacity and add an EU region. Also hoping to lower per-token costs w some batching optimizations, but latency needs to stay under 250ms p50 for short prompts.
[01:41] Rajiv: to add, we have compliance obligations in EU for a vertical customer. we need SOC two artifacts, audit logs, and we prefer a VPC/private control plane for the EU workloads. not necessarily full on-prem yet.

[02:08] Maya: Okay makes sense — we usually offer dedicated pools for predictable throughput and a private/VPC control plane for residency. quick question on traffic shape — tom, can you share current qps and typical sequence lengths?
[02:20] Tom: sure, um current baseline avg is 18 qps, with spikes to 85 qps during morning digest runs. sequences mostly 32-256 tokens, average 80 tokens, some long-tail to 1k for batch reports. we do rounding and truncation client-side.
[02:45] Owen: that helps. for those spikes, continuous batching and KV cache help a lot — though for EU region we'd want to size the pool so spikes don't degrade latency SLOs. also want to confirm whether edenware will accept multi-region fallback or needs strict geo-failover.
[03:03] Lena: prefer strict — EU data must stay in-region for the regulated customers. fallback to US is not allowed for those tenants.

[03:25] Maya: Understood. So two asks: committed capacity for global (or regional) plus an EU-only pool behind VPC. For the contract we can propose an amendment with a term extension + committed throughput buckets. We'll add a clause about region-specific routing and no cross-border fallback for the scoped tenant set.

[04:00] Sara: timeline — we need to see numbers next week to align internal finance and get PO out. is that feasible?
[04:08] Maya: yes — we'll send a revised quote by Tuesday. (uh) Owen will also share a benchmark checklist to make the pilot as efficient as possible.

[04:28] Rajiv: on security docs, can you share SOC2 and ISO docs and details on KMS integration? we have an internal KMS and HSM for key wrapping.
[04:38] Owen: absolutely — we'll share the security pack. we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations on the private plane — sorry private plane, private control plane — sometimes the transcript says privet but i mean private. For hosted we do offer envelope encryption and you can bring your own key for certain Private deployments.

[05:10] Tom: important to call out egress charges — if we replicate logs to an EU SIEM there are transfer costs. also, how do you handle audit logs access for our compliance team?
[05:22] Maya: audit logs are available via the Console with retention tiers; we can keep them in-region for EU private deployments. egress for logs depends on storage choices; we'll include estimates in the revised quote.

[05:45] Owen: from a perf angle, quick note: long sequences (1k) change cost model and can increase latency. we recommend model quantization + batching for most flows, and keep the long reports in an async job path. we can suggest quantized model variants for cost savings if acceptable.

[06:15] Lena: would quantization affect accuracy on our summarization use-case? 
[06:20] Owen: small risk — usually we see <2% drop on rouge/bleu for summarization with 8-bit calibrated quant, but we can run evals on your prompt set during the pilot. we'll flag any regressions in the evals.

[06:45] Rajiv: also curious about throttling and QoS per route — we need token-level budgeting per customer. can you expose that?
[06:54] Maya: yes, Console supports per-route quotas and token-level billing. you can set per-tenant rate limits and routing policies. we'll include a sample config.

[07:18] Tom: ops question: for VPC private pilot, what is the provisioning lead time?
[07:22] Owen: dev VPC provision is typically 5-7 business days if network peering and subnets are straightforward; for a production-grade EU cluster expect 3-4 weeks including legal and KMS setup.

[07:45] Sara: okay, so for our PO timing if we get the quote on Tuesday we could probably cut a PO in two weeks, but legal needs a draft amendment first. can you draft the amendment or do we need internal redwood legal touchpoints?
[07:58] Maya: we can draft a contract amendment (standard SOW + capacity addendum) and share it. we'll mark the parts that typically require negotiation (SLA, data residency clause, indemnity).

[08:20] Lena: for the pilot, scope suggestion: 1) small EU-only pool with 10 reserved GPUs for 2 weeks; 2) run 2-hour benchmark with our representative traffic; 3) run evals on 500 prompt/pair sets. sound reasonable?
[08:34] Owen: yes, that's a good starting point. we suggest also capturing KV cache hit rates and prefix reuse so we can tune batching and cache TTL.

[08:56] Tom: what about fallback strategies if the EU pool is saturated? we need clear behavior — queue, rate-limit, or degrade to smaller model?
[09:05] Maya: we can define a policy: for scoped tenants we will not failover to US; instead, the policy options are queueing with backpressure, shed to a smaller quantized model variant in-region, or return a 429. we should pick a primary behavior — many customers choose in-region model degrade to preserve data residency.

[09:36] Rajiv: prefer in-region degrade to smaller model. but we need metrics to trigger it. can that be automated?
[09:42] Owen: yes — automatic fallback to a pre-approved model variant with a controlled temperature/response change is supported; we'll show a sample rollout policy.

[10:10] Lena: on pricing: are there discounts for commit term length? 12-month vs 6-month? also, do you price regional pools separately?
[10:20] Maya: yes; higher commitment yields better unit pricing. regional pools are either isolated reservations (priced per-region) or you can buy global commit and allocate by policy — we'll show both options in the quote. typical structure: base commit (global) + region add-on (EU) + burst credits.

[10:40] Sara: we need clear egress and storage estimates included. last renewal had surprise charges.
[10:46] Maya: noted — we'll include sample egress scenarios and storage tiers.

[11:05] Owen: small transcription note, earlier you asked about KV cache management: our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we can set cache affinity per-route so EU tenants use EU cache nodes only (to avoid cross-border cache replication). sometimes the automatic transcript writes KV cash but it's KV cache.

[11:35] Tom: good. about the pilot benchmarks — will you run them on our schema? we usually have a custom tokenizer and a pre-tokenization step.
[11:42] Owen: yes we can run using your pre-tokenizer; helpful if you can provide a 2k sample payloads with real headers. Owen will provide the exact format in the benchmark checklist.

[12:05] Maya: next — legal sensitive items: retention period for logs, delete-on-request, and subprocessor list. we'll include those in security pack.
[12:14] Rajiv: subprocessor list is important. also interested in separate SLA for EU pool.

[12:30] Maya: we'll propose an EU-specific SLA. if the EU pool is part of Dedicated or Private, SLA options increase.

[12:50] Lena: one blocker: our procurement wants a single vendor for both hosting and monitoring; do you have integrations for Datadog / Splunk?
[12:59] Owen: yes — we integrate with Datadog and Splunk for metrics and logs; for Private we can forward logs directly to your SIEM within the VPC; for hosted we can push via secure pipelines.

[13:20] Sara: can you provide sample invoices or billing run-rate so finance can forecast?
[13:27] Maya: yes — sample billing scenarios included in the quote and we'll map to your forecast inputs.

[13:40] Lena: technical question — how do you handle model rollbacks if a new model variant regresses on our prompt set? we need automatic rollback tied to eval thresholds.
[13:50] Owen: we have rollout controls and quality monitoring; canary deploys and automated rollback if eval metrics drop beyond agreed thresholds. we'll set up a prompt-set based eval during the pilot and configure alerts.

[14:10] Maya: okay, time check — we have about 30 more minutes. any other sticking points?
[14:18] Rajiv: two more: backup/restore for the Private control plane, and attachable HSM; and second, want to ensure SSO integration with our Okta.
[14:28] Owen: we support Okta SAML SSO and RBAC mapping. Private control plane supports customer-managed KMS and HSM for key wrapping. backups can be in-region and we can document restore RTO/RPO.

[14:55] Tom: on-side note — do you support A/B testing routing so we can split a small percent to a cheaper model variant for a subset of customers?
[15:03] Owen: yes, per-route A/B traffic splitting and percentage-based rollouts are supported in our routing policies. good for cost experiments.

[15:25] Lena: perfect. for the pilot dates the week of May 10 works for our infra team. can you commit to reserved dev pool by May 12 as you mentioned earlier?
[15:35] Maya: we can aim for May 12 for dev VPC provision; production-grade EU cluster later. we'll put that in the next steps.

[15:50] Sara: procurement will need a contract redline within a week — will that be possible?
[15:55] Maya: we'll produce a draft amendment by Friday, May 7, with highlighted negotiable sections.

[16:10] Owen: a couple of quick technical caveats: if you plan to use long-tail 1k tokens in high qps mode we'll recommend async workers to keep p50/p95 latency good. also if you want quantized models we should run evals first.

[16:36] Tom: understood. Owen, can you include recommended batching and cache TTL defaults for our traffic pattern in the checklist?
[16:41] Owen: yes will add heuristics for batch size, max latency window, and cache TTLs.

[17:05] Lena: competitor note — some teams asked if Anthropic or VoltAI were easier for EU data residency; can you summarize differences?
[17:13] Maya: briefly — some competitors offer region-specific managed hosting but vary on BYOK and private control plane maturity. we'll add a short comparison in the follow-up, but focus should be on cost/latency and certs.

[17:35] Rajiv: last question: will we get a single point of contact for onboarding?
[17:40] Maya: yes I'll be your AE and Owen will be your SE for the pilot. we'll also assign a customer success lead once we execute the amendment.

[17:58] Sara: thanks, that helps.

[18:05] Maya: ok quick recap and next steps — We'll: 1) Send revised quote + sample billing scenarios by 2026-05-05; 2) Draft contract amendment by 2026-05-07; 3) Owen to send benchmark checklist same day; 4) Edenware to provide traffic samples and confirm PO owner by 2026-05-06 / 05-10; 5) target dev VPC provision by 2026-05-12 and run pilot week of May 10.

[18:36] Tom: thanks everyone. we'll get the samples over.
[18:40] Lena: appreciate it.
[18:45] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up in email and log action items.

[18:55] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: medium — a few mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g. "privet" for private), KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash, occasional filler words retained.
